candidates.entry: At month-end, compute trailing 12-month dividend yield for each ETF in the universe; rank them. Go long the top 3 yield ETFs and short the bottom 3 yield ETFs. Enter positions at the next day open.
candidates.exit: Close all positions at the next month-end (i.e., hold for ~1 month).
candidates.sizing: Allocate equal dollar amount to each long and short leg; target portfolio volatility of 8% annualized using a rolling 60-day volatility estimate of the long-short spread.
candidates.regime_filter: Skip the month if the 30-day realized volatility of SPY (proxy for market risk) exceeds 20% or if the 60-day SPY momentum is negative.
candidates.rationale: Citation 1 shows a carry factor built from sector ETFs delivers a Sharpe ~0.65; using dividend yield as a proxy for carry should capture a similar return premium while keeping correlation low to momentum/value, aiming to clear Tier-2 floors.

candidates.entry: Compute the daily spread S = XLF_price - XLE_price. Calculate its 60-day rolling mean μ and standard deviation σ. When S < μ - 2σ, go long XLF and short XLE; when S > μ + 2σ, go long XLE and short XLF. Enter at next day open.
candidates.exit: Close the pair when the spread reverts to within 0.5σ of μ or after a maximum holding period of 20 trading days, whichever comes first.
candidates.sizing: Risk-scale each trade to target 1% of portfolio equity per pair, using the 20-day rolling volatility of the spread to set position size.
candidates.regime_filter: Skip trading on days when the VIX (proxy from ^VIX) exceeds 30 or when the 10-day average volume of either ETF falls below its 30-day median (liquidity filter).
candidates.rationale: Citation 2 documents that ETF arbitrage exploiting NAV deviations yields Sharpe 0.7-1.0, especially in XLF and XLE; a spread-mean-reversion proxy captures similar mispricing without needing NAV data.

candidates.entry: At month-end, compute 60-day total return for each ETF in the universe. Rank them and go long the top 4 performers, short the bottom 4 performers. Enter at next day open.
candidates.exit: Rebalance monthly; close all positions at month-end and re-enter based on updated rankings.
candidates.sizing: Allocate equal capital to each long and short leg; apply a portfolio-level volatility target of 10% annualized using a 60-day rolling volatility of the long-short basket.
candidates.regime_filter: Skip the month if the 30-day realized volatility of the MSCI World Index (proxy via VTI) exceeds 18% or if the 60-day momentum of the S&P 500 is negative.
candidates.rationale: Citation 3 finds cross-asset momentum across sector ETFs yields Sharpe 0.6-0.8; a simple monthly ranking implementation should capture the same effect while providing diversification across sectors.

candidates.entry: For each ETF, compute (a) trailing 12-month dividend yield and (b) 60-day total return. Standardize both metrics across the universe and sum to obtain a combined score. Go long the top 3 scoring ETFs and short the bottom 3. Enter at next day open after month-end ranking.
candidates.exit: Hold positions for 30 calendar days or until the combined score rank changes by more than 2 positions, whichever occurs first.
candidates.sizing: Equal dollar allocation per leg; scale to a target portfolio volatility of 9% annualized using a 30-day rolling volatility of the long-short spread.
candidates.regime_filter: Skip the month if the 20-day average VIX exceeds 28 or if the 30-day realized volatility of the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index (proxy via BND) exceeds 10%.
candidates.rationale: Combining the carry (yield) signal from citation 1 with the momentum signal from citation 3 should produce a more robust factor, leveraging low correlation between the two sources to improve risk-adjusted returns.

candidates.entry: Go long any ETF whose 60-day total return is positive at month-end; otherwise stay in cash.
candidates.exit: Reassess monthly; exit any position whose 60-day return turns negative.
candidates.sizing: Allocate up to 100% of capital to the single longest-positive-momentum ETF; if none, stay fully in cash.
candidates.regime_filter: Skip the month if the 30-day realized volatility of SPY exceeds 22% (high-vol regime) to avoid noisy signals.
candidates.rationale: A simple momentum-only approach tests whether the documented cross-asset momentum premium persists after 2020; if backtest fails to meet Tier-2 thresholds, it suggests the edge has decayed for retail traders.

notes_to_p3: Focus on monthly rebalancing and volatility-scaled sizing; ensure data quality for dividend yields (use yfinance 'dividends' field) and for spread calculations. Verify regime filters using external volatility proxies (VIX, SPY realized vol) to avoid overtrading in turbulent periods.
